predecessors.name: Kingdom of Georgia
predecessors.text: Kartli around Tbilisi, ruled by Bagrat VI as King of Kartli-Imereti 1466-1478 until Constantine II 'challenged him'; Cliopatria draws it as its 'Kingdom of Georgia' row (27,616 km2 in 1468-1506)

successors.name: Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti
successors.text: the Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti, into which Kartli merged in 1762 ('Union of Kartli and Kakheti: 1762'); Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Georgia' row, 54,778-55,276 km2 for 1763-1802

ledger.x: 1478: Constantine II founds the Kingdom of Kartli at Tbilisi.
1632: Persia sets Rostom Khan over Kartli.
12 June 1723: an Ottoman army takes Tbilisi.
1736: the Ottomans give up Kartli and Kakheti.
1762: Erekle II unites Kartli and Kakheti.
1762: the Kingdom of Kartli ends in the Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti.

wars.name: Ottoman-Safavid War (1578-1590)
wars.outcome: Lala Mustafa Pasha took Tiflis in August 1578 and pressed Kartli to become a tributary; by the treaty of 21 March 1590 the Safavids ceded 'parts of Georgia' among much else.

wars.name: Ottoman-Safavid War (1603-1618)
wars.outcome: Safavid armies captured Tbilisi in 1603-1604 and 'both Kartli and Kakheti became Safavid dependencies once again'; the Treaty of Nasuh Pasha (20 November 1612) 'secured the 1555 borders envisaged by the Peace of Amasya', i.e.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines on the pages; the frontiers of Kartli with Samtskhe, Imereti, Kakheti and the Persian and Ottoman lands are approximate.
